target_customer: Law firms (first logos are Nordic firms), plus banks, investment firms, consultancies and life sciences companies doing document-heavy work
problem: Transactional lawyers and similar professionals spend hours checking and redlining documents in Word and email. Vesence puts quality-assurance agents inside Microsoft Word and Outlook, later widening to an agent-native computer.
product_category: Legal AI review agents and agent workspace

founders.name: Henrik Hansson
education: Studied physics and economics at two Swedish universities at the same time (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Previously a music producer with tens of millions of streams per the YC page. Worked at Depict alongside the founder of Lovable.

founders.name: Ludvig Swanström
founders.background_notes: YC page says Forbes 30 Under 30 and former professional basketball player. Founders say they have known each other for eight years.

competitors.name: Spellbook
competitors.what: AI contract drafting and review assistant inside Microsoft Word
competitors.traction_then: Word-native option used by corporate legal teams and mid-size firms

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable review inside Word and Outlook requires Office add-in engineering and precision tuning, but built on commercial models.

defensibility.rationale: Embedding in firm workflows adds friction to switching, but Spellbook and others already served Word and larger platforms could add similar review.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying documented in sources checked through 2026.

market_need_then: Legal teams were adopting AI drafting tools in 2025; Vesence's pitch is checking existing work rather than generating content.

branding.domain_note: Uses vesence.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short punchy fragments, confident, e.g. One person. One screen.

branding.brand_signature: Cursor for transactional lawyers launch framing

brand_strength.rationale: Legal tech press covered the raise; the name is easily confused with the Vessence spelling of unrelated brands.

outcome_analysis: Vesence raised a $9M seed in October 2025, months after its YC Spring 2025 batch, led by Emergence with Creandum, YC and 20VC. The raise reflects strong investor interest in legal AI delivered inside Office, backed by well-connected Swedish founders. It has since broadened toward Excel, PowerPoint and an agent workspace. No distress or exit found.
notes: Creandum calls the round pre-seed while other outlets call it seed; recorded as seed. One listing gives 7.7M euros; ZoomInfo names YC as lead, conflicting. The Spellbook page is vendor-authored. Founded year not stated by a source. Education of Ludvig not found.
